title: edilint diff JSON report, version 1
description: The document `edilint diff --json` writes: one structural comparison of two X12 files. The `version` field is incremented, and a new schema file committed, whenever a consumer written against the previous version could meet something it has not seen before.

version.description: The document shape version. This schema describes version 1.

a.description: The first input path as given, "-" for standard input.

b.description: The second input path as given, "-" for standard input.

strict.description: Whether cosmetic differences were compared as well.

identical.description: True when no differences were found at the requested strictness, which is what exit status 0 means.

differences.description: One entry per difference, in envelope order. Always an array, [] for identical files.

difference.description: A single structural difference between the two files.

kind.description: What differs. The *-added kinds mean the construct is only in the second file, the *-removed kinds only in the first.

cosmetic.description: Present and true for differences that only strict comparison reports: terminator style, and values that differ only in trailing whitespace.

designator.description: The conventional X12 element designator, e.g. "CLP03". Present only for element differences.

a.description: The differing content from the first file: the element value, the terminator and its padding, or the segment or envelope-header text of a removed construct. Empty when the first file lacks the construct.

b.description: The differing content from the second file, with the same meaning as "a".

a_line.description: The 1-based physical line of the segment involved in the first file. Absent when the first file lacks the construct.

b_line.description: The 1-based physical line of the segment involved in the second file. Absent when the second file lacks the construct.

message.description: A one-line human-readable description carrying the path.

path.description: Where the difference sits in the envelope hierarchy. Every index is 1-based and names a position, not a control number. Positions refer to the first file, except that a construct present only in the second file is located by its position there. Segment is the position within its enclosing unit; for a transaction set that is the ST-through-SE ordinal, so ST is segment 1.

transaction_type.description: ST01 of the transaction set, e.g. "835".

element.description: The X12 element position, so CLP03 is element 3.

summary.description: Difference counts by disposition. Cosmetic counts the differences only strict comparison reports, whatever their kind, so it overlaps the other counters.
